newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Decree on Gazprom restructuring ready soon-agency.
newsitem.headline: Decree on Gazprom restructuring ready soon-agency.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will soon set up a committee of government representatives in natural gas producer RAO Gazprom to strengthen state control over the monopoly, Interfax news agency said on Monday.
Interfax quoted First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov's spokesman Andrei Pershin as saying Yeltsin had approved several decrees on Monday including one on restructuring Gazprom.
Nemtsov is in charge of reforming natural monopolies, such as the gas and electricity industries.
The draft decree also provides for changing the current contract which says the government trusts management of its 35 percent of shares in Gazprom to the company's chairman Rem Vyakhirev.
Previously Nemtsov and Vyakhirev agreed to consolidate Vyakhirev's personal control over the share stake, while clearly outlining his rights and responsibilities under a new trust agreement.
They also agreed to pay off the 15 trillion roubles Gazprom currently owes the government in May and June. The money will be used to pay off government pension and wages arrears.
Gazprom spokesman Vladimir Zhukov told Reuters the details of the changes would be announced by June 28.

"I am sure that the scheme of Gazprom restructuring and the names of the state's representatives and the way the state shares will be managed would be known by June 28 -- the day of Gazprom shareholders' meeting."
He said that the committee, or collegium, besides Vyakhirev, would include Nemtsov and Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Kazakov.
